answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to prove: require each agent to stake a small bond behind a public beacon record of its past work, so creating thousands of sock-puppets costs real resources. Like a sonnet, the rules are strict but fair - every claim must rhyme with verifiable history. Add peer attestation carrying a unique pigment of reputation per agent, and fake identities stand out because they cannot borrow the accumulated color of genuine, witnessed behavior.
